I turn methods from my research into open-source R packages so they can be used directly in established pharmacometric software.

::: card-grid
::: tile
![](assets/images/pmxNODE-sticker.webp){fig-alt="pmxNODE hex sticker"}

### pmxNODE {#pmxnode}

Use low-dimensional neural ODEs inside your structural models. pmxNODE translates NN functions into the equations required by **Monolix, NONMEM, and nlmixr2**.

```r
install.packages("pmxNODE")
```

Paper: [Bräm et al. 2025, CPT:PSP](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13265) ·
[CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pmxNODE) ·
[GitHub](https://github.com/braemd/pmxNODE)

Taught at workshops in Hong Kong (2026), Uppsala (2026), and Copenhagen (2025).

[Tutorials →](tutorials/pmxNODE/index.qmd){.tile-link}
:::

::: tile
### optiDoseR {#optidoser}

Estimate optimal doses that fulfil predefined therapeutic targets. optiDoseR generates the model code and data for the OptiDose approach in **Monolix, NONMEM, and nlmixr2**.

```r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("braemd/optiDoseR")
```

Paper: [Bräm et al. 2025, J Clin Pharmacol](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.6188) ·
[GitHub](https://github.com/braemd/optiDoseR)

OptiDose workshop at PAGE (2023).

[Try the interactive dose optimiser](tools/dose-optimiser.qmd) to see the principle live in your browser.

[Tutorials →](tutorials/optiDoseR/index.qmd){.tile-link}
:::
:::
